author: TEDx Talks
description:
Psychotherapist and Couple Expert Stan Tatkin argues that when couples fight, the real issue is almost never what they're fighting about — it's what happens in their nervous systems when either partner is under stress. Drawing on decades of clinical work, he shows how our brains mistake prediction for danger, turning the people we love into perceived threats. His answer isn't more love, but a consciously designed relationship: shared purpose, agreed-upon principles, and a plan for repair before the next conflict even arrives.

 tan Tatkin, PsyD, MFT, is a clinician, researcher, teacher, and developer of A Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy® (PACT). He has a clinical practice in Calabasas, CA. With his wife, Dr. Tracey Tatkin, he co-founded the PACT Institute for the purpose of training other mental health professionals worldwide, along with a growing PACT faculty, to use this method in their clinical practice. Together, Stan and Tracey also lead couple workshops.

title: Why love alone can't save your relationship | Stan Tatkin | TEDxKC

description:
Most of us eventually learn how to save money — but almost none of us learn how to teach it. In this talk, Mark Schlipman and Steve Short reveal why 85% of Americans over 45 wish they'd started saving sooner, and argue the real problem isn't knowledge, it's habit. Using a simple budgeting framework and the same logic you'd use to teach a kid to brush their teeth, they lay out a system parents, mentors, and employers can use to help the next generation build financial literacy and savings habits early — before they ever have the chance to fall behind.

 Steve Short is a retired C-suite executive, strategic advisor, and co-author of the best-selling personal finance book The Simple Road Toward Financial Freedom. He spent nearly 30 years at Enterprise Holdings, where he rose from Management Trainee to Vice President, ultimately leading a $3B+ division and helping drive more than $2B in growth through innovation, partnerships, and customer-focused strategy.

title: You don’t have a savings problem. You have a system problem. | Steve Short & Mark Schlipman | TEDxKC

description: Digital systems architect Ken Cardwell opened his TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk by asking the audience to imagine a deepfake video of themselves, saying and doing things they never said or did, created entirely from photos and clips they had already posted online. What followed was not a warning about technology. It was an argument about identity itself. Drawing on his patents in synthetic identity binding and his work building governed systems for digital presence, Cardwell closes with the line that gives the talk its title: identity comes before output. Ken Cardwell is a founder and systems architect working at the intersection of identity, artificial intelligence, and human representation. He is the founder of ActorForge and the Virtual Actors Guild, where he is building early infrastructures for governed synthetic performers—digital entities designed to operate with defined identity, consent, authorship, and lifecycle control. description: How do you move on after a tragedy? In this talk, Joyce Ng shares three simple ways to transform personal hardship into a life of purpose. As a survivor of the 9/11 attacks and also a student at Brown University during the mass shooting, Joyce discusses her experiences on how to live with purpose that can be distilled into eleven words. Beyond her career, her most profound impact lies in her advocacy. As the founder of a nonprofit supporting the 9/11 community and author of the history book Hotel 9/11, she has transformed her experience of survival into a lasting legacy of support and historical preservation. description:
Esta charla aborda uno de los momentos más difíciles dentro de la atención en salud: comunicar una mala noticia a un paciente.
Desde la perspectiva de quien tiene la responsabilidad de transmitir esa información, se explora cómo una noticia puede cambiar la vida de una persona y por qué la manera en que se comunica puede ser tan importante como el mensaje mismo.
A través del protocolo SPIKES, se presentan herramientas para comunicar malas noticias de una forma más empática, humana y respetuosa, considerando no solo la información médica, sino también las emociones, necesidades y dignidad de quien la recibe.
Porque detrás de cada diagnóstico hay una persona, una historia y una vida que merece ser escuchada y acompañada. Médico cirujano por la Universidad Autónoma de Coahuila y médico residente de Angiología y Cirugía Vascular y Endovascular en la UMAE No. 34 del IMSS en Monterrey. description: Understanding others begins with listening, communication, and questioning how we perceive the world around us. This talk explores why people turn to conspiracy theories, how these narratives simplify a complex and often unfair reality, and what happens when we stop trying to understand one another. Valentin Valkanov, PhD, is a sociologist and Assistant Professor in the Department of Philosophy and Sociology at New Bulgarian University. His research focuses on propaganda, conspiracy theories, media, and public attitudes. His doctoral dissertation explores post-truth and conspiracy narratives in healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic. He is also a research fellow at the Human and Social Studies Foundation – Sofia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
